items.rule: First-year project budget between $500,000 and $20 million
items.quote: NOAA will not accept proposals with a first year budget less than $500,000 or more than $20 million under this solicitation.

items.rule: Not a federal, state or tribal government
items.quote: Applications from federal, state, or tribal governments will not be considered, due to their potential role as trustee council members.

items.rule: If a local government, identifying large-scale opportunities based on current or anticipated restoration plans
items.quote: Applications from local governments will only be considered if they identify potential large scale restoration opportunities based on current or anticipated restoration plans.

items.rule: Registered with SAM.gov and holding a Unique Entity Identifier
items.quote: Applicant organizations must first register with SAM.gov and obtain a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) that will be used throughout the application process.

items.rule: If applying online, registered with SAM.gov, eRA Commons and Grants.gov before submitting
items.quote: Applicant organizations and individuals must register for three different Federal systems prior to submitting an application through Grants.gov (SAM.gov, eRA Commons, and Grants.gov).

items.rule: Cooperating with NOAA to reduce or avoid identified adverse environmental impacts
items.quote: Applicants will also be required to cooperate with NOAA in identifying feasible measures to reduce or avoid any identified adverse environmental impacts of their proposal. Failure to do so shall be grounds for not selecting an application.

items.rule: No judgment lien for unpaid U.S. government debt, unless DOC waives the restriction
items.quote: Pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 3201(e), unless waived by DOC, a debtor who has a judgment lien against the debtor’s property for a debt to the United States is not eligible to receive any grant

answer.notes: The 2026 NOFO controls over older general guidance. It also allows local governments subject to the stated restoration-plan condition, a category missing from the supplied listing. The NOFO says it does not anticipate accepting total federal requests below $2.5 million or above $100 million; this qualified wording is not treated as a categorical eligibility rule. Staffing, previous federal awards, clean audits and broad geographic reach are evaluation criteria or preferences. Selected applications also undergo Grants Office administrative and risk review and pre-award negotiations; the notice does not specify their relative order. Summary and narrative are recommended; CVs and letters of support are optional. Other optional supplemental materials include indirect cost rate agreements, restoration planning documents and work plans; supplemental information is limited to 40 pages. The NOFO gives October 30 for semiannual reports, while general NOAA award conditions say October 31. Audit thresholds differ: $1 million in annual federal expenditures for entities covered by Subpart F, versus $1 million in annual DOC expenditures for commercial and other excluded entities unless award terms specify otherwise; the latter may submit a GAGAS financial-related audit or a project-specific audit. Subaward reporting generally applies at $30,000, with a stated exemption for recipients whose previous-year gross income was below $300,000. Property reporting is conditional on relevant property; real-property reporting can use longer intervals for federal interests lasting 15 years or more. Training requirements apply to personnel at NOAA facilities or covered vessel crews. Award-specific conditions are supplied with the award.
